summary: Frontend-only testing of new GRID mode at /grid. All 10 functional requirements passed: route loads with grid-stage rendering 303/MTL/PLUGIN tokens + IDX-### metadata block; Restructure button and Space key change IDX (207→214→221); Palettes (red/bw/blue) toggle active state AND change stage background color (rgb(255,30,30) / rgb(10,10,10) / rgb(30,50,255)); Invert & Flip-on-cut toggles switch ON/OFF; BPM auto-loop restructures automatically when playing (IDX 207→270 over ~2s at BPM=220 cutEvery=1) and Stop halts it; count slider grows cells (4→13); grid-text-input tokens propagate; title/subtitle inputs update meta; font-select changes span fontFamily (Archivo Black→Anton); pop-out opens /grid-output with a clean grid-stage rendered; mode-kinetic navigates to / and mode-grid returns to /grid.
critical_code_review_comments: Media clips are stored as blob: URLs from URL.createObjectURL — these are opaque to the pop-out window; the pop-out receives the clip metadata via BroadcastChannel but cannot resolve the blob URL (different origin/document). Consider streaming the media via captureStream to a shared MediaSource or serializing images to base64 for cross-window rendering. Not blocking for text/meta workflow, but the 'Pop-out for capture into Resolume' claim is partial when media clips are used.

GridStudio.jsx keydown effect depends on [restructure, config.flipOnCut] but calls setConfig via the flipOnCut branch — fine, but the 'f' fullscreen key and 't' tap key handlers are also declared inside the same effect; consider extracting to reduce re-binds on every config.flipOnCut change.

buildScene idxCode uses Math.abs(Math.imul(seed,7)) % 800 + 200 — there is a small collision chance across consecutive seeds; visually acceptable but a monotonic counter would guarantee uniqueness per cut.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All GRID mode UI/interaction requirements verified through live browser automation against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Kinetic mode was not retested per request. No backend involvement for /grid.
